title: Loops
test_conventions: Tests are Python assert snippets executed AFTER the learner's code, in the same namespace, one snippet at a time. Everything the learner's code printed is available to tests as the string variable __stdout__. expected_output comparisons are exact after stripping trailing whitespace on each line (and trailing blank lines). tests[].visible defaults to true; visible:false tests are hidden and always carry a failure_message. For fill_blank, blanks in starter_code are written ___ and are filled in order; every alternative in blanks[].answer must pass the tests. For parsons, lines are shown shuffled; correct_order lists, for each position of the solution, the index into lines; distractors are extra lines that must not be used. For predict, expected_output must be one of choices; for debug with expected_output the fixed program's stdout must match it exactly. The learner source code is available to tests as the string __source__.

notes: The body repeats while the condition is True.

exercises.explanation: count becomes 1 and prints 1. At 2, continue skips the print. At 3 it prints. At 4, break ends the loop before printing.

misconceptions.1\n3\n4: break runs when count is 4, before the print line.
misconceptions.0\n1\n3: count is increased BEFORE the print, so 0 is never printed.

tests.failure_message_tr: Döngü sınırı değişebilir: kodun yalnız 3'ü atlayıp diğer sayıları yazdırmaya devam etmeli.

hints: Add an if inside the loop that handles count == 3.
continue skips the rest of the round, but count must still grow first, or the loop never ends.
Put an if before the print: when count is 3, increase count by 1 and then use continue.

solution.approach: Increase count and continue when count is 3, before the print.
solution.code:
count = 0
while count < 5:
    if count == 3:
        count += 1
        continue
    print(count)
    count = count + 1
solution.approach_tr: count 3 iken önce count'u artır, sonra continue kullan; hepsi print'ten önce olsun.

hints_tr: Döngünün içine count == 3 durumunu ele alan bir if ekle.

print'ten önce bir if koy: count 3 ise count'u 1 artır ve sonra continue kullan.

notes: for takes each item of a sequence in turn.

misconceptions.Mia\n30\nname Mia\nage 30: Looping over the dictionary directly gives the KEYS, not the values.
misconceptions.name\nage\nMia 30: items() gives each key together with its value, so each line starts with the key.
misconceptions.name Mia\nage 30\nname\nage: The loops run in the order written: first the keys, then the pairs.

notes: range(start, stop, step) stops BEFORE stop.
A counter or total outside the loop collects results.

misconceptions.3\n6\n9\n[5, 3, 1]: range starts at its first argument, 0, which is printed.
